Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Machine Learning, Data Engineering, Fraud Operations, and Risk to improve fraud strategies, strengthen operational feedback loops, and support new product launches.

EXPERIENCE - 7+ years’ of Analytics experience

EXECUTION - Able to thrive in a fast-paced environment and be responsive and available during times of peak fraud activity

The Director, Information Technology & Security will serve as a key member of the Bank's Management Team, serving as the Chief Information Security Officer, and will be responsible for establishing and leading the Bank's information security and cybersecurity programs. As the Bank prepares to launch as a de novo Industrial Loan Company (ILC), this leader will design and implement an enterprise-wide security framework that meets FDIC and state regulatory expectations, supports the Bank's risk appetite, and protects customer and institutional data.
This is a blended leadership role requiring both high-level strategic influence and deep technical execution. You will lead the development of information security governance, technical controls, and oversight of infrastructure and engineering, ensuring a strong and scalable security posture from inception. This leader must be a practitioner at heart—willing to "roll up their sleeves" to lead the technical build phase, collaborate closely with engineering on architecture, and ensure security is integrated into every aspect of the Bank's systems and operations.
What You’ll Do
Oversee infrastructure design and IT Engineering
Information Security Program Development
Design, implement, and maintain a comprehensive Information Security Program consistent with FDIC guidance (e.g., FIL-66-2019, FIL-13-2021) and the Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards.
Develop and oversee policies, standards, and procedures governing cybersecurity, data protection, and incident response.
Ensure alignment with the Bank’s overall risk management and governance frameworks.
Provide regular reporting to executive management and the Board on the Bank’s security posture, emerging risks, and mitigation efforts.
Lead the technical build phase of the Bank's infrastructure, providing direct oversight and hands-on guidance for cloud security and DevOps integration.
Partner deeply with Engineering to define and implement secure technical architectures, including network segmentation, encryption standards, and identity governance.
Cybersecurity and Threat Management
Establish and manage a threat monitoring and detection capability to identify, assess, and respond to cybersecurity risks.
Oversee implementation of layered security controls (e.g., network segmentation, encryption, access controls, endpoint protection, vulnerability management).
Lead the Bank’s Incident Response Program, ensuring timely escalation and coordination with regulators when required.
Maintain relationships with information-sharing groups (e.g., FS-ISAC) and law enforcement to stay informed of emerging threats.
Third-Party and Affiliate Risk Oversight
Evaluate the information security posture of third-party and affiliate service providers in accordance with the Bank’s Vendor Management Program and FDIC third-party risk guidance.
Establish due diligence, ongoing monitoring, and contractual requirements for vendors handling sensitive data or performing critical services.
Coordinate with Operations, Compliance, and Internal Audit to ensure third-party risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated.
Manage the technical lifecycle of security-critical third-party service providers, ensuring rigorous operational oversight of vendors handling sensitive financial data.
Data Governance and Privacy Protection
Ensure compliance with applicable privacy and data protection requirements (e.g., GLBA, Regulation P, state privacy laws).
Implement processes to safeguard customer information and prevent unauthorized access, disclosure, or misuse.
Partner with business and technology teams to integrate privacy-by-design principles into new products and services.
Business Continuity and Resilience
Assist Risk Officer in development and testing of the Bank’s Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plans, ensuring they are integrated with information security objectives.
Coordinate regular testing and simulations to validate readiness for cyber incidents and system disruptions.
Support resilience planning for key systems, vendors, and communication protocols.
De Novo and Pre-Opening Readiness
Build and document the Bank’s technology and information security program as part of the de novo application process.
Establish security architecture, monitoring tools, and vendor relationships prior to launch.
Prepare readiness materials for FDIC and state examinations related to cybersecurity and operational resilience.
Ensure security risk assessments and third-party reviews are completed and incorporated into pre-opening milestones.
Leadership and Culture
Serve as the Bank’s senior advocate for cybersecurity and data protection, promoting a culture of security awareness and accountability.
Provide training and guidance across the organization to enhance information security awareness.
Collaborate with peers in Risk, Compliance, Operations, and Technology to align security priorities with business strategy.
Build and lead a capable, mission-driven security team to support the Bank’s evolving needs.
What We Look For
Minimum of 10 years of experience in information technology, and security and technology risk management, with a proven track record of moving between strategic planning and hands-on technical execution.
Demonstrated experience designing and implementing information security programs compliant with FDIC and FFIEC standards.
Strong familiarity with third-party risk frameworks and financial services cybersecurity expectations.
Experience leading incident response, penetration testing, and security operations in cloud-based and hybrid environments.
Proven ability to communicate complex technical topics to executive leadership, the Board, and regulators.
Strong leadership, analytical, and problem-solving skills with a risk-based and pragmatic approach to decision-making.
Deep expertise in cloud-native infrastructure (AWS/GCP), DevOps practices, and software-defined security controls.
Demonstrated ability to "roll up sleeves" and contribute directly to the technology build while simultaneously managing executive stakeholders and regulators.
Core Competencies
Expert knowledge of information security principles, frameworks, and regulatory requirements.
Strategic thinker with strong operational execution and control discipline.
Effective communicator capable of influencing across technical and business functions.
Collaborative leader who fosters a culture of accountability, awareness, and continuous improvement.
Affirm Values
At Affirm, we live by our values: People Come First, No Fine Print, It’s On Us, Simplify, and Push the Envelope. As CCO, you will embody these principles while building the foundation of Affirm Bank as a trusted, transparent, and innovative financial institution.

Consumers across the globe need safe, transparent financing while merchants want to provide users with their preferred way to pay and convert more buyers. To help achieve this vision, we are hiring a Senior Product Manager for our 1:Many Growth team.
Affirm's Distribution Partnerships program - internally called " 1:Many " - is one of the highest-leverage growth levers at the company. Instead of integrating merchant by merchant, we integrate once into a platform merchants already use, and every merchant on that platform becomes reachable through that single integration. This role is responsible for:
Own and grow Affirm's partner portfolio - making it easier and more frictionless for merchants to onboard and offer Affirm as a payment method to their customers. This includes taking product ownership of Affirm's existing vertical software partnerships, and growing the broader portfolio of platform partners still being stood up.
Partner Acceleration Strategy - building the durable capabilities that make every future partner integration faster to launch and easier to scale, rather than solving the same problem one partner at a time.
As a Senior Product Manager, you will work closely with cross-functional teams including commercial, merchant risk, design, product analytics, and engineering to define, launch and grow integrations with platform partners. Effective stakeholder management and ability to successfully navigate organizational dynamics are a must for success. You should be outcomes-driven with a very high bias for action.
What You'll Do
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define, launch, and grow integrations with payment and platform partners.
Build durable, repeatable capabilities through a Partner Acceleration Strategy that makes future partner integrations faster to launch.
Build relationships with platform partners to gather feedback and insights on product performance, and use it to drive merchant growth.
Define and prioritize product features and requirements to improve the customer, partner, and merchant experience.
Create and manage the product roadmap for the broader 1:Many growth team.
Develop success metrics/OKRs to measure the effectiveness of these initiatives.
Partner with commercial and product marketing teams to develop go-to-market strategies for new partner integrations and features.
What We Look For
5+ years of product management experience
Proven ability to multiple technical software products from kickoff to post-launch, driving meaningful business impact you can clearly articulate.
Skilled in cross-functional collaboration — diving into technical details with engineers, iterating with designers in Figma, and analyzing funnel performance with data analysts.
Strong organizational and communication skills to navigate complex dynamics and drive alignment.
Execution-oriented with a proactive approach to overcoming obstacles and blockers.
Adept at transforming incomplete or conflicting inputs into clear, actionable plans.
Demonstrated track record of shipping high-quality products on time.
Comfortable engaging in the commercial aspects of product development, including representing the product externally, setting expectations, and influencing outcomes that benefit both Affirm and its partners.
Bonus points: Experience in Fintech, Lending, ecommerce, or BNPL.

You have 7+ years of experience designing, developing and launching backend systems at scale using languages like Python or Kotlin.

Integrate CIAM platforms with internal systems, including user data stores, messaging, fraud signals, and downstream customer platforms.
Own secure authentication and account flows end to end, including MFA, step-up authentication, device binding, consent, and adaptive authentication logic.

Strong production experience in Python or a similar backend language
Experience designing APIs, automation frameworks, and distributed systems
Hands-on experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines
Experience with GitHub-based development workflows and Buildkite or similar build systems
Experience with cloud-native development, preferably AWS
Hands-on experience extending and integrating CIAM platforms such as Okta, Auth0, Ping Identity, ForgeRock, or Azure AD B2C using custom code, hooks, and APIs.
Solid understanding of backend and distributed systems fundamentals, including API design, data modeling, latency, error handling, and observability.
Experience with Infrastructure as Code and automation tools such as Terraform, plus CI/CD pipelines for deploying backend services.
Strong security fundamentals applied through engineering, including access control models, token handling, encryption, MFA, and privacy by design.

Familiarity with tools such as Cursor and other AI-augmented development environments

About the Role
Affirm is building its own bank — and this role is one of the most senior individual-contributor seats on the engineering team that runs it. We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to be a technical anchor for a deliberately small, AI-native team that owns the systems behind Affirm's bank: vendor-integrated banking infrastructure, the data platform, and the operational tooling that holds it all together. You'll set technical direction across that surface area, own the hardest problems on the team — including the Bank ↔ Affirm Inc integration boundary — and operate with direct exposure to senior bank and Affirm leadership.
This is a rare opportunity to shape a new business from its very first systems — a startup-like build inside an established company — at a level of ownership that goes beyond delivering your own projects. As a Staff engineer here you set the bar: the architecture, the standards, and the technical strategy that the rest of the team builds against. The team is small and AI-native, the surface area is broad, and the decisions you make carry far — every system you ship serves real customers under a real bank charter, and the patterns you establish determine what the bank becomes.
What You'll Do
Set technical direction across the bank's systems. Own the medium-to-long-term technical strategy for the bank's core surfaces — cloud infrastructure, data platform, core banking configuration, CI/CD, networking, and the Bank ↔ Affirm Inc integration — and make the architecture calls the rest of the team builds against. Generalist breadth is expected; you go deep where the risk is highest.
Own the hardest problems end-to-end. Personally design, build, integrate, and operate the most ambiguous and highest-stakes pieces of the stack, and own incident response for them. You take the problems no one else can fully scope and turn them into well-defined systems with clear failure domains, monitoring, and runbooks.
Be the force multiplier on a small team. Set and hold the bar for code review, design review, and examiner-readable documentation. Establish the patterns and standards that let a deliberately small team punch far above its size, and level up every engineer who joins after you.
Ship AI-first, and push the frontier of it. Treat AI tools and agentic workflows as a load-bearing capability for code, design review, runbook generation, and operations — and actively push yourself and the team on what an AI-leveraged engineering function can deliver in place of additional headcount.
Lead vendor selection and ownership. Drive evaluation, integration, and ongoing oversight of the bank's third-party platforms across the core, data, identity, observability, and card-processing stacks. Carry the bank's most critical vendor relationships end-to-end: integration, operations, escalation, and audit.
Define the integration boundary with Affirm Inc. Set the domain edges, data flows, and integration patterns between the bank and Affirm Inc so the bank's products work seamlessly inside the Affirm ecosystem while preserving the legal and regulatory separation the charter requires. Drive this across Affirm Inc engineering teams whose systems integrate with the bank's.
Build for examiners. Partner with Legal, Compliance, Risk, BSA/AML, Finance, and Internal Audit so compliance is a property of the product from day one. The systems you design are the artifacts FDIC and state examiners will inspect — design and document them to a standard that holds up under examination and audit review.
Own the operational posture of the bank's systems. Set the reliability, observability, alerting, runbook, incident-response, and disaster-recovery practices that keep the bank standalone-operable and audit-ready, while keeping the operational footprint intentionally small. You will support the operations and availability of your team’s artifacts by creating and monitoring metrics, escalating when needed, and supporting “keep the lights on” & on-call efforts.
Influence up and across the organization. Communicate technical strategy, tradeoffs, and constraints with clarity to bank executives, the Bank Board, Compliance, Risk — and to engineers outside the bank across the broader Affirm org. The relationships you build beyond the team shape how cleanly the integration boundary works.
Help grow the team and the bar. As engineers join, they inherit a function whose architecture, practices, and standards you helped set. Mentor peers, provide high-signal feedback, contribute to hiring, and lead by example.
What We Look For
8+ years of software engineering experience, with staff-level, hands-on builder credentials and a track record of owning ambiguous, high-stakes systems end-to-end through launch and operations
Comfortable owning ambiguity at the largest scale on the team — you move fast, make the tough prioritization calls, take ownership before being asked, and balance speed with the engineering judgment the hardest decisions require
Hungry to leverage AI to drive outcomes — fluent with AI-assisted development tools (Claude, Cursor, Codex, agentic workflows) and actively pushing yourself and your team to use them as a multiplier for code quality, velocity, and what a deliberately small team can ship
Bias toward simplicity — experience building toward a small, lean engineering culture that rewards "buy over build", a default-deny posture, and standalone-operability over an abundance of tooling
A track record of setting technical direction — you've defined architecture and multi-quarter technical strategy for systems beyond your own projects, and led the execution of it across engineers and teams without needing a management title to do so
Deep systems thinking across public cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), infrastructure-as-code (Terraform), and cloud data platforms (Snowflake or comparable) — you understand their failure modes and tradeoffs, not just their surface APIs
Regulated-environment experience — direct work in banking, payments, securities, healthcare, or another setting subject to external examination, where the work involves examiner-facing documentation and decisions
Direct experience selecting, integrating, and operating meaningful third-party platforms under operational ownership after launch
Comfortable as the technical face of the work to non-engineering stakeholders — bank executives, the Board, Compliance, Risk, Finance, and examiners — and able to document decisions so they hold up under audit review
Exceptional written and verbal communication — you can distill complex technical, regulatory, and operational concepts into clear narratives for executives, boards, and non-engineering audiences
This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field
Nice to have
Prior work inside a bank, neobank, Banking-as-a-Service provider, card issuer/processor, or fintech with a chartered bank subsidiary
Direct experience with a de novo bank launch, an early-stage bank buildout, or a greenfield regulated platform
Hands-on experience with a bank core, card processing / issuer processor integration, or digital bank experience integration
Hands-on experience standing up a greenfield cloud organization — fresh cloud org, IAM model, and data platform — under a tight, default-deny security posture
Familiarity with the regulatory framework that shapes the work: FDIC examinations, GLBA / Reg P (affiliate data sharing), BSA/AML, Reg E, Reg DD, Reg Z, model risk, and third-party risk management
